title: The Down Under Lounge
venue_description:
About The Down Under Lounge

The Down Under Lounge stands as one of Omaha's most beloved neighborhood bars combining an intimate dive bar atmosphere with a commitment to live music and inclusivity. Since its establishment the venue has built a reputation as a safe welcoming space for people of all backgrounds with particular recognition as an LGBTQIA-friendly establishment.

Live Music and Entertainment

Music is at the heart of The Down Under's identity. The 100-capacity venue hosts live performances Wednesday through Saturday featuring local and regional artists across diverse genres. Wednesday nights belong to the DU Open Mic one of the longest-running open mic nights in Omaha. Originally hosted by singer-songwriter Aly Peeler the night is now led by Mad Darling welcoming musicians poets comedians puppeteers live painters and other performers for three-song sets. The event starts at 7 PM with no cover charge and features drink specials making it accessible to both performers and audiences.

Beyond open mic nights the venue showcases established local bands and touring artists Thursday through Saturday. The intimate setting creates an energetic atmosphere where audiences and performers connect in meaningful ways. Tuesday nights feature karaoke adding another dimension to the weekly entertainment lineup.

Drinks and Atmosphere

The Down Under Lounge takes pride in its beverage program featuring over 45 beers available on tap and in bottles and cans. The bar is particularly known for its award-winning Bloody Mary vodka infusions with 4-5 seasonal rotating flavors. They also serve Krupnik a centuries-old Polish tradition of honey vodka infused in-house. The bartending staff has earned consistent praise for exceptional customer service with regulars noting that bartenders remember orders even after single visits.

Community and Culture

What sets The Down Under apart is its strong sense of community. Patrons describe the atmosphere as positive and uplifting with a crowd that's equally welcoming and supportive. The venue has cultivated a reputation where everyone feels like family - newcomers are greeted with open arms while regulars consider it a second home. The staff is consistently praised for being kind amazing and creating a five-star service experience.

Located at 3530 Leavenworth Street the venue is easily accessible in central Omaha. Hours run from 3 PM to 2 AM Monday through Sunday with live entertainment typically starting around 7-8 PM. The venue features flexible seating that can be rearranged to accommodate different types of events from intimate acoustic performances to dance-heavy shows. An outdoor patio provides additional space for socializing.

Booking and Events

The Down Under Lounge welcomes artists interested in performing and can be contacted for booking inquiries. The venue's commitment to supporting local artists and providing a platform for emerging talent has made it an essential part of Omaha's music ecosystem. Whether you're looking to perform for the first time or catch a show by established local favorites The Down Under Lounge delivers an authentic neighborhood bar experience with a genuine love for music and community.

title: Dubliner Pub
venue_description:
About Dubliner Pub

Dubliner Pub brings authentic Irish pub culture to Omaha's historic Old Market district operating in a landmark building with a rich history dating back to 1894. The building originally served as a tack supply business and later housed a mannequin manufacturing company before finding its calling as one of Omaha's premier Irish establishments.

Historic Setting

In 1978 Paul McGill purchased the John A. Horbach building which was designated an Omaha landmark in 1979 and is now listed in the National Register of Historic Places. McGill developed Horbach's in the basement space that once served as coal intake and storage eventually renaming it Dubliner Pub to emphasize its authentic Irish character. The current owners Vance and Cindy who also operate Cohen & Kelly's Lounge in West Omaha acquired the pub in 1999 and have maintained its reputation as the closest thing to a traditional Irish pub this side of the Atlantic.

Music and Entertainment

Live music is central to the Dubliner Pub experience with performances scheduled throughout the week. The pub hosts two distinct open mic nights - Monday evenings feature comedy with tight five-minute sets and a pre-show writing workshop while Wednesday nights shift focus to music giving singer-songwriters and bands opportunities to test new material or jam with regulars. Live Irish music fills the pub on Fridays and Saturdays with additional performances on Tuesdays and Thursdays featuring local and regional artists.

Food and Drink

True to Irish pub tradition Dubliner Pub specializes in Irish whiskey and maintains an extensive selection of authentic Irish beers including Guinness Harp Smithwicks and Powers. The pub offers daily happy hour from noon to 7 PM with $1 off drinks. Special nightly promotions include Irish Night on Mondays with $4 Guinness Harp Smithwicks and Powers from 7 PM to close Tuesday features $5 Red Bull drinks and $3 Corona Wednesday offers $4 well drinks Thursday brings $5.50 pitchers of PBR and Sunday is Service Industry Night running from 7 PM to close.

Private Events and Venue Rental

The Dubliner Pub's basement event space can accommodate up to 100 guests making it ideal for receptions bridal showers dinners corporate meetings and other special occasions. The venue provides an affordable option in the heart of the Old Market with the charm and character of a historic building. For corporate gatherings the pub offers a projector and screen to support presentation needs. Live entertainment can be arranged for events and the pub works with clients on decorating to match their vision whether casual pub ambiance or more formal sophisticated settings.

Location and Hours

Located at 1205 Harney Street in the Old Market the pub is open Monday through Saturday from noon to 2 AM and Sundays from 1 PM to 2 AM. The basement location creates an intimate underground atmosphere perfect for enjoying traditional Irish hospitality while experiencing Omaha's vibrant local music scene.

title: North Omaha Music and Arts
venue_description:
About NOMA

North Omaha Music and Arts (NOMA) represents a transformative vision for music education and cultural preservation in Omaha. Operating from the historic Love's Jazz and Arts Center building at 2510 N 24th Street NOMA occupies a space steeped in the rich jazz heritage of North Omaha's legendary 24th Street corridor where jazz greats once performed in venues like the Dreamland Ballroom in the Jewell Building.

Mission and Leadership

Founded and led by Executive Director Dana Murray a native Omahan and former drummer for Grammy-winning artists Norah Jones and Wynton Marsalis NOMA is dedicated to providing world-class musical instruction in a cultural context to youth and adults in Greater North Omaha and surrounding communities. The organization's mission focuses on stimulating growth and development through access to professional resources and perspectives that might otherwise be unavailable due to economic barriers.

Educational Programs

NOMA offers comprehensive curricula in music dance and music production with particular emphasis on jazz blues funk soul and improvisation. The academy features state-of-the-art facilities including dedicated labs for piano broadcasting bass percussion and other instruments. Classes are designed for both youth and master-level adult players with programs that deep dive into the technical and creative aspects of performance and composition.

The organization's educational philosophy emphasizes that while not every student will pursue music professionally the skills developed through musical training - discipline focus collaboration creative thinking - are transferable to any career path. As Murray notes the academy aims to develop not just great musicians but also future doctors lawyers businesspeople and community builders.

Performance Opportunities and Events

NOMA serves as both an educational institution and a performance venue hosting live jazz showcases jam sessions concerts and special events throughout the year. Monday nights feature jazz-heavy open jam sessions while Wednesdays spotlight Omaha's underground music scene. Both nights begin with live performances by accomplished musicians followed by free open jam sessions from 7-10 PM encouraging collaboration between experienced players and emerging talent.

The academy's signature event is NOMAFEST an annual jazz festival held at Turner Park that brings world-renowned artists to Omaha. The 2025 lineup featured Eric Gales Ghost-Note Lakecia Benjamin Heidi Martin and Dana Murray & Manifesto showcasing top-tier talent in blues funk and jazz genres. NOMAFEST celebrates the legacy of the jazz musicians who once made 24th Street a cultural epicenter while nurturing the next generation of artists.

Facilities and Future Vision

NOMA underwent significant expansion in 2025 adding new labs and facilities to support its growing programs. The long-term vision includes a 450-seat music venue and what would be the largest recording studio in Omaha - a $20 million project designed to create a comprehensive music and arts destination. These planned improvements will provide students and professional musicians alike with world-class resources for learning performing and recording.

Community Impact

Beyond music education NOMA plays a vital role in community development and cultural preservation. By revitalizing the former Love's Jazz building and honoring the area's musical heritage the organization helps catalyze economic entrepreneurial and entertainment opportunities in North Omaha. The academy has hosted master classes with legendary musicians including John JR Robinson the most recorded drummer in history demonstrating its commitment to bringing exceptional talent and learning opportunities to the community.

Philosophy and Values

NOMA operates on core principles including the belief that opportunity can change lives that education is a lifelong pursuit and that hard work and discipline unlock human potential. The organization emphasizes equitable access to quality music education regardless of economic circumstances while maintaining professional standards and cultural context in all programming. Through this approach NOMA enriches and empowers the community creating a destination venue that attracts world-class talent while developing local artists.

title: The Nifty Bar
venue_description:
About The Nifty Bar

The Nifty Bar proudly carries the distinction of being Benson before Benson was Benson having served the community since the 1930s. This quaint neighborhood bar has maintained its character through decades of change offering a genuine old-school watering hole experience in northwest Omaha's Benson area.

Atmosphere and Ambiance

The Nifty embodies the spirit of a classic neighborhood bar where regulars and newcomers alike feel welcomed into a familial atmosphere. The venue brings together a diverse mix of patrons from college students to longtime residents creating a truly intergenerational community space. Despite being a smaller intimate venue The Nifty's vibrant personality shines through in every detail from the colorful decor to the warm welcoming service.

The bar features multiple entertainment options including pool tables darts and life-sized Jenga providing plenty of activities for socializing. An outdoor covered patio extends the space allowing guests to enjoy Nebraska weather while maintaining the cozy neighborhood vibe. The venue has a back-alley entrance adding to its authentic dive bar character and sense of local discovery.

Drinks and Specialties

The Nifty takes particular pride in its beverage program focusing on local craft beers both on tap and in bottles and cans. The bartending staff - often referred to as knowledgeable encyclopedias of alcohol - expertly craft cocktails with margaritas earning special recognition as dangerously good. The bar serves local and regional spirits alongside its beer selection ensuring a well-rounded menu for all preferences.

Happy hour runs Monday through Friday from 4-7 PM featuring $2 pints and $2 well drinks making it an ideal spot for after-work gatherings. While the food menu is limited The Nifty offers select snacks including pizzas and nachos for guests who get peckish during their visit.

Live Music and Events

Music plays a significant role in The Nifty's weekly programming. Every Wednesday the bar hosts a rotating open mic night led by different local artists inviting performances of all kinds. The setting is cozy and intimate with a warm supportive crowd that makes performers feel at ease. Sign-ups happen in person so arriving early is recommended to secure a slot.

Beyond open mic nights The Nifty features live bands once a month showcasing various genres and local talent. The venue also hosts weekly quiz nights adding intellectual competition to the entertainment mix. These regular events combined with the welcoming atmosphere make The Nifty a hub for community connection and cultural engagement.

Community and Culture

What sets The Nifty apart is the genuine sense of community it fosters. As patrons frequently note it's the kind of place where after just a visit or two everyone knows your name. Regulars speak highly of both the clientele and the bartending staff creating an environment where new friendships form naturally and old ones are celebrated.

The Nifty's location on Northwest Radial Highway places it slightly off the main Benson strip but regular patrons consider this a feature rather than a drawback. The venue attracts those seeking an authentic neighborhood bar experience away from more touristy areas. Sports fans appreciate the TVs while music lovers enjoy the quality sound system and intimate performance space.

Practical Information

The Nifty Bar operates with hours that accommodate both early evening gatherings and late-night socializing. Monday and Tuesday the bar is open from 2 PM to midnight while Wednesday through Saturday hours extend from 2 PM to 2 AM with Sunday running from noon to midnight. The venue's size makes it perfect for intimate gatherings though its popularity means weekends can get busy.

For those new to the area or visiting Omaha The Nifty represents one of the city's best-kept secrets - a genuine neighborhood bar that maintains its character and community focus while welcoming all who walk through the door. Whether stopping in for a quick drink during happy hour catching the weekly open mic or settling in for a full evening of pool and conversation The Nifty delivers an authentic unpretentious bar experience.

title: Shakedown Street Tavern
venue_description:
About Shakedown Street Tavern

Shakedown Street Tavern continues the proud musical legacy of its location in downtown Benson carrying forward traditions established when the building housed the beloved Barley Street Tavern. The venue stands as a testament to Benson's evolution into a creative district while maintaining the authentic dive bar character that made the original space so special.

Grateful Dead Heritage

As the name suggests Shakedown Street Tavern draws inspiration from the Grateful Dead creating a space where Deadheads and music lovers gather to celebrate live music and community. The venue's identity is deeply rooted in the improvisational collaborative spirit of the jam band tradition making it a natural home for open-ended musical exploration and diverse performances.

The OG Open Mic

Shakedown Street's Monday night open mic has earned legendary status as the OG (original) open mic in Omaha. While not continuous throughout the venue's history the tradition has been passed down through generations of hosts predating even the regular live music programming at the location. Current host Brixz Gonzaba who began leading the night in May 2022 maintains an informal walk-up format where performers simply show up - no advance sign-ups required.

The open mic typically draws between 5-15 performers per night creating an intimate unpredictable experience. The event takes place in the venue's familiar side room a space that has witnessed countless performances over the years. Musicians performing original Americana material mix with comedians testing new jokes and covers artists tackling songs by Tyler Childers and similar artists. This eclectic mix creates the anything-can-happen atmosphere that makes open mics so compelling.

Live Music Programming

Beyond the Monday open mic Shakedown Street Tavern hosts live music performances nightly featuring local and regional artists working in folk jazz blues pop and jam band genres. The venue has become an essential stop for touring acts passing through the Omaha area while also providing a platform for established local favorites to connect with dedicated audiences.

The tavern's programming reflects the Benson Creative District's commitment to fostering artistic expression and cultural vitality. Shows typically range from intimate solo performances to full band productions with the venue's sound system and intimate layout ensuring quality experiences regardless of the night's lineup.

Benson Creative District

Shakedown Street Tavern's location at 2735 N 62nd Street places it in the heart of downtown Benson a neighborhood that has transformed into one of Omaha's premier arts and entertainment destinations. The Benson Creative District designation recognizes the area's concentration of galleries performance spaces restaurants and bars that collectively create a vibrant cultural ecosystem.

The tavern participates in district-wide events like Benson First Friday contributing to the neighborhood's reputation as a must-visit destination for arts and culture. The venue's proximity to other Benson establishments makes it easy to experience multiple facets of the district's offerings in a single evening.

Atmosphere and Vibe

Shakedown Street maintains the authentic dive bar atmosphere that defines Benson's music venues - unpretentious welcoming and focused on the music rather than flashy production. The intimate side room creates natural connections between performers and audiences while the main bar area provides space for socializing and enjoying drinks between sets.

Regular patrons and performers appreciate the venue's commitment to keeping music accessible and authentic. There's no pretense here just good music good people and the kind of communal experience that makes live music special. The space welcomes artists of all experience levels creating opportunities for first-time performers to take the stage alongside seasoned veterans.

Community Role

As one of the few venues maintaining a regular open mic tradition Shakedown Street Tavern plays a crucial role in Omaha's music ecosystem. Open mics serve as the backbone of any thriving music community providing testing grounds for new material opportunities for artistic growth and entry points for emerging talent. The tavern's commitment to this programming helps ensure that Omaha's music scene continues to develop and flourish.

The venue's connection to Barley Street Tavern's legacy also provides continuity for longtime music fans who remember the original venue's importance to the community. By honoring that history while creating new memories Shakedown Street Tavern bridges generations of Omaha music lovers.

title: Brokedown Palace
venue_description:
About Brokedown Palace

Brokedown Palace represents a unique convergence of musical influences combining the flower power ethos of the Grateful Dead with the passionate sports culture of Nebraska Cornhuskers football. This unlikely but surprisingly successful pairing creates a bar atmosphere that welcomes diverse crowds united by love of live music good drinks and community.

Concept and Atmosphere

Founded by two veteran bartenders and childhood friends Brokedown Palace emerged from a vision to create a space celebrating both the improvisational collaborative spirit of the Grateful Dead and the pride of Nebraska football. The venue features extensive Dead and Huskers memorabilia including concert posters an autographed helmet and local art creating a visually rich environment. A large aquarium and trippy visual projections add to the eclectic comfortable atmosphere.

The bar's layout balances intimate performance space with traditional bar functionality. The front area features couches and comfortable seating creating a living room feel perfect for enjoying music while the back maintains a more conventional bar setup. This dual nature allows the venue to accommodate both focused listening experiences and casual socializing.

Weekly Entertainment Schedule

Brokedown Palace hosts an impressive lineup of weekly events making it a seven-nights-a-week destination for entertainment seekers. Every Monday from 8-10 PM Eva Bleu Band takes the stage delivering raspy soul and fuzzy funk riffs described as Janis Joplin floating through a Dead set tangled in purple haze and moonlight. These shows feature no cover charge with $2 Busch Lite cans and $2 Bud and Bud Lite draws.

Tuesday nights combine open mic and Taco Tuesday starting at 6 PM with $1 tacos $3 Modelos and $5 margaritas. The open mic runs from 8 PM to midnight offering 15-minute performance slots for music comedy and poetry. Current host Spidercat welcomes sign-ups via direct message or in person. This night has earned particular recognition from local musicians as a well-run supportive open mic experience.

Wednesday brings karaoke hosted by Zach Kurmel one of Omaha's finest entertainers running from 8 PM to midnight. Thursday nights feature live music performances and Ladies Night from 4 PM to close. A unique Thursday addition is Patio Flow - a weekly gathering from 7 PM to midnight welcoming hoopers poi spinners jugglers drummers aerial artists and flow enthusiasts for open jam sessions under the stars. This event creates a festival atmosphere celebrating movement and rhythm.

Food and Drink

The bar maintains competitive pricing with daily happy hour from 3-6 PM featuring rotating specials. The Tuesday Taco specials have become particularly popular combining affordable food with quality entertainment. Brokedown Palace serves a full selection of craft beers both local and regional along with well-crafted cocktails and standard bar offerings.

A unique feature is the venue's connection to Homestyle Cafe accessible through a Dutch door allowing guests to order breakfast or lunch directly into the bar. This partnership extends the venue's food options beyond typical bar snacks creating a more complete dining experience.

Special Events and Streaming

Brokedown Palace regularly hosts special events including Grateful Dead tribute shows livestreams of Dead & Company performances and themed celebrations. The venue streamed all three nights of Dead & Company's 60th Anniversary shows from Golden Gate Park in August 2025 offering big screen visuals and full sound with no cover charge. These events attract dedicated Deadheads from across the region creating community celebrations around shared musical passion.

The bar also celebrated New Year's Eve 2026 with live music heavy hors d'oeuvres by chef Natelina Mickles and a complimentary champagne toast demonstrating its capacity to host special occasion events.

Pet-Friendly Policy

Brokedown Palace welcomes dogs making it a favorite destination for pet owners. The bar provides water bowls and creates a welcoming environment for patrons' four-legged friends adding another dimension to its inclusive community-focused approach.

Location and Access

Located at 8805 Maple Street just east of 90th Street on the Maple Street frontage road Brokedown Palace sits adjacent to Homestyle Cafe amid convenience stores and light industry. While the location might seem unassuming the venue has become a destination worth seeking out. Hours typically run from 11 AM to 2 AM though specific times may vary by day.

Community and Culture

Patrons consistently praise Brokedown Palace's friendly atmosphere affordable drinks and welcoming vibe. The diverse clientele includes Deadheads sports fans music lovers and neighborhood regulars creating a genuinely inclusive environment. The venue's commitment to live music multiple times per week combined with its unique thematic identity has established it as an essential part of Omaha's music scene particularly for those seeking jam band culture and improvisational musical experiences.

title: American Legion Hall Post #1
venue_description:
About American Legion Hall Post #1

American Legion Hall Post #1 serves as the home venue for the Great Plains Bluegrass & Old-Time Music Association (GPBOTMA) providing a community gathering space for traditional music preservation and performance. Located at 7811 Davenport Street two blocks north of Dodge just west of 78th Street the hall offers an accessible central location for music lovers across the Omaha metro area.

Great Plains Bluegrass & Old-Time Music Association

GPBOTMA has dedicated over 40 years to preserving and promoting bluegrass and old-time music in Nebraska. The organization holds monthly meetings at American Legion Hall Post #1 from October through May creating a seasonal rhythm that brings together musicians and music fans throughout the colder months when indoor venues become particularly valuable.

Each first Sunday afternoon from 2:00-5:00 PM the hall hosts a structured program featuring a one-hour live band performance followed by open jam sessions. This format allows attendees to enjoy professional-quality performances before participating in collaborative music-making. The jam sessions welcome musicians of all skill levels from beginners learning their first tunes to experienced players who have been jamming for decades.

Admission and Accessibility

GPBOTMA maintains affordable admission rates to ensure accessibility for all community members. Members pay $3 while non-members pay $5 with children 12 and under admitted free. This pricing structure supports the organization's mission of keeping traditional music alive and accessible while maintaining sustainable operations.

Musical Tradition

The association's focus encompasses both bluegrass and old-time music - related but distinct American folk traditions. Bluegrass with its driving rhythms instrumental virtuosity and high harmonies developed in the mid-20th century while old-time music represents earlier Appalachian string band traditions. GPBOTMA celebrates both styles honoring the full spectrum of American acoustic roots music.

The organization celebrated its 40th anniversary with special events including outdoor performances at Venelyst Park demonstrating its commitment to bringing traditional music to diverse audiences. Past anniversary celebrations have featured groups like the Dirty River Ramblers and local family bands like The Kopsas who have recorded at Tesco Productions.

Community Impact

By providing regular gathering opportunities GPBOTMA helps preserve musical traditions that might otherwise fade while creating intergenerational connections between experienced musicians and younger players. The jam session format encourages learning through participation as less experienced musicians can follow along with standard bluegrass and old-time tunes while developing their skills.

American Legion Hall Post #1's partnership with GPBOTMA demonstrates how community organizations can support cultural preservation and artistic development. The hall provides the physical space and infrastructure needed for regular gatherings while GPBOTMA brings the programming expertise and community connections that make these events meaningful and sustainable.
